###Read data
```{r}
#csv needs to be in the same folder as the Rmd file
#getwd()

eventdata <- read.csv(file = 'cyber_event_binned_data.csv', 
                      stringsAsFactors = F)

binnedCount <- eventdata$event.count
binnedLen <- eventdata$avg.report.length
weekvar <- eventdata$week

count.data <- cbind(weekvar, binnedCount, binnedLen)

colnames(count.data) <- c("Time", "Counts", "Length")
count.data  <- data.frame(count.data)
t <- weekvar
```

###Index of dispersion (I) and histogram

```{r, warning = TRUE, echo = TRUE}

#Index of Dispertion (var/mean[rate])
counts <- count.data$Counts

#Variance
var(counts)

#Mean
mean(counts)

I <- var(counts)/mean(counts)
I
```

###Bursts: Figure 3
```{r, warning = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
nweeks <- length(binnedCount)
offsets <- numeric()

for (i in 1:nweeks){
    
    tempweek <- i-1 #i want to start with 0
    tempcount <- binnedCount[i]
    
    temparrivaltimes <- seq(from = tempweek, by = 1/tempcount, length.out = tempcount)
    
    offsets <- c(offsets, temparrivaltimes)
    }

bursts <- kleinberg(offsets)

# make the x-axis show times instead of the time index variable
timevar <- c(weekvar, tail(weekvar, 1) + 1:50)

yr1 <- 16
yrchange <- seq(from = yr1, to = tail(timevar, 1), by = 52)

plot.burst.cyber <- function (x, ...)
    {
    max_level <- max(x$level)
    plot(c(), type = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "Burst Intensity (Level)", bty = "n",
         xlim = c(1, 400), ylim = c(1, max_level), axes = FALSE,
         yaxt = "n", ...)
    axis(side = 1, at = yrchange, labels = paste("Year", 1:8), tick = T)
    axis(2, at = 1:max_level, las = 2)
    arrows(x$start, x$level, x$end, x$level, code = 3, angle = 90,
           length = 0.05)
    }
 
plot.burst.cyber(bursts)
dev.copy2pdf(file="plots/Fig3_bursts.pdf", width = 9, height = 6)
dev.print(png, "plots/Fig3_bursts.png",    width = 9, height = 6, 
          units = 'in', res = 600)
dev.off()
```

###Bayesian state space model using Stan with brms 
```{r, warning = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
head(count.data)

set.seed(9999)
fit1 <- brm(Counts ~ Time, data = count.data, autocor = cor_bsts(formula = ~1), 
            family = negbinomial, iter = 12500, control = list(max_treedepth = 15)) 
fit1
plot(fit1, ask = FALSE)

set.seed(9998)
fit2 <- brm(Counts ~ Time + Length, data = count.data, autocor = cor_bsts(formula = ~1), 
            family = negbinomial, iter = 12500, control = list(max_treedepth = 15))
fit2
plot(fit2, ask = FALSE)

#Model Comparison: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1507.04544.pdf
#Widely Applicable Information Criterion (WAIC) 
summary(fit1, waic = TRUE)
summary(fit2, waic = TRUE)
```

####Typical time-series model: AR1 and AR3
```{r, warning = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
#make a variable for the structural break
sb <- c(rep(0, 83), rep(1, length(binnedCount) - 83))

# seasons <- quarter(weekvar) #seasonality - this was not significant, leaving it out
# seasons <- paste("q", seasons, sep = "")

#residuals of this model are the detrended time series, use this going forward
count.lm <- lm(binnedCount ~ t + sb)
dt.count <- resid(count.lm)

#may also want to try to use detrended report length as predictor:
len.lm <- lm(binnedLen ~ t + sb)
dt.len <- resid(len.lm)


# first, look at acf and pacf of time series
# if it's just AR or MA, you can kind of figure it out from that
# if it's ARMA, it's a little harder

acf(dt.count)
pacf(dt.count)

#visually, I would guess maybe an AR(3), since the acf has a slow decay, and
#the pacf has spikes to lag 3

ar3 <- arima(dt.count, order = c(3,0,0))
print(ar3)

#try auto.arima. this should give us the best ARIMA model. it does its own unit
#root testing and looks for drift and seasonality, so it will also be a good 
#check on our detrending and unit root testing above
arima.mod <- auto.arima(dt.count)
print(arima.mod)

#try auto.arima. this should give us the best ARIMA model. it does its own unit
#root testing and looks for drift and seasonality, so it will also be a good 
#check on our detrending and unit root testing above

arima.mod <- auto.arima(dt.count)
print(arima.mod)

# doesn't use an intercept - maybe because detrending by definition centers the
# time series around 0? 
# No "I" term - that's good, confirms what we already thought
# This method says AR(1) and MA(1). Seems plausible. Need to test residuals to 
# make sure this model accounts for all the serial correlation

# NOTE: we can also add some external predictors to the model (IR length)
# I did this, and it didn't add anything: arima(dt.count, order = c(1,0,1), xreg = dt.len)

#Check residuals
res <- arima.mod$residuals

# need to see if there's still any serial correlation
acf(res)
pacf(res)

#test residuals against whitenoise
LjungBoxTest(res, k = 1)

# no strong evidence of serial correlation remaining

#test for normality
shapiro.test(res)
qqnorm(res)
qqline(res)

# seems pretty non-normal. this was true of all the models I tried. this is 
# problematic, but not as concerning as residual serial correlation would be.
# worth mentioning as limitation - possible that log transform of data would
# address this
```

####Measures of trend forecast accuracy: All data and bursts (L3 and L2)
```{r, warning = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
#AR1 (untrended) forecast trendline: est.ar1 = AR1

#make a function to UNDETREND x-values
 undetrend <- function(x, t, sb, lm.mod) 
    {
     coefs <- lm.mod$coefficients
     preds <- coefs[1] + coefs[2] * t + coefs[3] * sb
     return(x + preds)
    }

armapreds <- fitted(arima.mod)
est.ar1   <- undetrend(armapreds, t, sb, count.lm)

armapreds2 <- fitted(ar3)
est.ar3   <- undetrend(armapreds2, t, sb, count.lm)

#Drop the weeks with 0 observed events
#Weeks 5, 62, 75 
counts.no.zero   <- rbind(eventdata[1:4,], eventdata[6:61,],
                     eventdata[63:74,], eventdata[76:366,])

ar1.est.no.zeros <- c(est.ar1[1:4],   est.ar1[6:61], 
                     est.ar1[63:74], est.ar1[76:366])


ar3.est.no.zeros <- c(est.ar3[1:4],   est.ar3[6:61], 
                      est.ar3[63:74], est.ar3[76:366])

#BSSM 
#est = forcase trend line for all weeks
BSSM.est.no.zeros <- c(est[1:4],   est[6:61], 
                       est[63:74], est[76:366])

#Measures of Forecasting Accuracy: MAE, MAPE, and sMAPE
#Forecast accuracy function
forecast.accuracy <- function(fitted.values.zero, fitted.values)
  {
  MAE      <- sum(abs(counts-fitted.values))/length(counts)
  
  #Removed zeros MAPE (otherwise divide by zero)
  MAPE     <- (1/length(counts.no.zero$event.count)) * 
               sum(abs(counts.no.zero$event.count  - fitted.values.zero)/counts.no.zero$event.count)
  
  MAPE.acc <- (1 - MAPE)*100
  
  sMAPE    <- 1/length(counts) * sum(abs(counts- fitted.values)/(counts + fitted.values))
  
  SMAPE.acc<- (1 - sMAPE)*100
  
  RMSE     <- sqrt(sum((fitted.values-counts)^2)/length(counts))
  
  forecast.accuracy.values <- t(cbind(MAE, MAPE.acc, SMAPE.acc, RMSE, MAPE, sMAPE))
  
  return(forecast.accuracy.values)
  }

AR1.acc  <- forecast.accuracy(ar1.est.no.zeros, est.ar1)
AR3.acc  <- forecast.accuracy(ar3.est.no.zeros, est.ar3)
BSSM.acc <- forecast.accuracy(BSSM.est.no.zeros, est)
model.comparison <- c("BSSM", "AR1", "AR3")
model.acc <-  cbind(BSSM.acc, AR1.acc, AR3.acc)
colnames(model.acc) <- model.comparison
kable(model.acc, digits = 2)

#Sanity check: accuracy() from the forecast package returns the same values
  accuracy(est.ar1, counts)

  #accuracy(ar1.est.no.zeros, counts.no.zero$event.count)

  #MAPE alone
  100-accuracy(ar1.est.no.zeros, counts.no.zero$event.count)[1,5]

#Forecast accuracy for bursts
#Bursts
  L3.bursts <- subset(bursts, level == 3)
  L2.bursts <- subset(bursts, level == 2)

#Extract weeks for L3 and L2 bursts into single vector
  L3.weeks <- c(L3.bursts$start, L3.bursts$end)
  L2.weeks <- c(L2.bursts$start, L2.bursts$end)

#Slice using the L3 and L2 weeks values:
#For observed data
  L3.obs <- as.matrix(data.frame(counts) %>% slice(L3.weeks))
  L2.obs <- as.matrix(data.frame(counts) %>% slice(L2.weeks))
  length(L3.obs)
  length(L2.obs)

#For fitted trendline data
  L3.BSSM <- as.matrix(data.frame(est) %>% slice(L3.weeks))
  L2.BSSM <- as.matrix(data.frame(est) %>% slice(L2.weeks))
  
  L3.ar1 <- as.matrix(data.frame(est.ar1) %>% slice(L3.weeks))
  L2.ar1 <- as.matrix(data.frame(est.ar1) %>% slice(L2.weeks))
  
  L3.ar3 <- as.matrix(data.frame(est.ar3) %>% slice(L3.weeks))
  L2.ar3 <- as.matrix(data.frame(est.ar3) %>% slice(L2.weeks))

forecast.accuracy.bursts <- 
  function(fitted.values, observed)
  {
  MAE      <- sum(abs(observed-fitted.values))/length(observed)
  
  MAPE     <- (1/length(observed)) * 
               sum(abs(observed  - fitted.values)/observed)
  
  MAPE.acc <- (1 - MAPE)*100
  
  sMAPE    <- 1/length(observed) * sum(abs(observed- fitted.values)/(observed + fitted.values))
  
  SMAPE.acc<- (1 - sMAPE)*100
  
  RMSE     <- sqrt(sum((fitted.values-observed)^2)/length(observed))
  
  forecast.accuracy.bursts <- t(cbind(MAE, MAPE.acc, SMAPE.acc, RMSE, MAPE, sMAPE))
  
  return(forecast.accuracy.bursts)
  }

#L3 bursts
  L3.AR1.acc  <- forecast.accuracy.bursts(L3.ar1, L3.obs)
  L3.AR3.acc  <- forecast.accuracy.bursts(L3.ar3, L3.obs)
  L3.BSSM.acc <- forecast.accuracy.bursts(L3.BSSM, L3.obs)
  L3.acc.table <- cbind(L3.BSSM.acc, L3.AR1.acc, L3.AR3.acc)
  colnames(L3.acc.table) <- model.comparison
  kable(L3.acc.table, digits = 2)
   
#L2 bursts
  L2.AR1.acc  <- forecast.accuracy.bursts(L2.ar1, L2.obs)
  L2.AR3.acc  <- forecast.accuracy.bursts(L2.ar3, L2.obs)
  L2.BSSM.acc <- forecast.accuracy.bursts(L2.BSSM, L2.obs)
  L2.acc.table <- cbind(L2.BSSM.acc, L2.AR1.acc, L2.AR3.acc)
  colnames(L2.acc.table) <- model.comparison
  kable(L2.acc.table, digits = 2)
```
